card.name: Start of a new term in drug tables
card.fires_on: Words that start a new term or phrase in drug label tables and lists, such as 'Con' at the start of contraindicate, concomitant or converting, and 'and' joining two condition names. Also 'patients' after 'observed in'.

modes.label: Con- at start of word
modes.description: The opening piece 'Con' of words like contraindicate, concomitant and converting, right after a drug name or heading.
modes.example: Ketoconazole<< Con>>traindicate coadministration of all potent

modes.label: 'and' between conditions
modes.description: The word 'and' joining two named infections in a dosing table.
modes.example: Hospital-acquired Bacterial Pneumonia<< and>> Ventilator-associated Bacterial Pne

modes.label: 'patients' after 'observed in'
modes.description: The word 'patients' in a side-effect sentence about observations in patients on therapy.
modes.example: have been observed in<< patients>> receiving antiretroviral therapy.

card.plain: It fires on the opening of a new term in drug tables, such as 'Con' in contraindicate or concomitant, and on 'and' between infection names.
